newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela reaches pay agreement with public sector.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela reaches pay agreement with public sector.

text.p: The Venezuelan government reached an agreement Tuesday with labor unions on a pay rise aimed at improving real salaries for public sector workers.

"The agreement shows that, if there is the will, it is possible in Venezuela...to reach understandings which avoid conflict," Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar was quoted as saying in a release.
Officials at the Finance Ministry and the Venezuelan Workers Confederation (CTV) -- the largest public sector union -- could not immediately say how large the pay rise was.
"It's a global agreement. It's not easy to say what it represents in percentage terms," CTV Secretary General Carlos Navaro told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.
Matos said the pay rise was above the inflation rate forecast for 1997. Government officials have said inflation is expected to be between 25 and 35 percent this year.
The government had originally offered Venezuela's 1.2 million public sector employees a 25 percent rise but this was later improved to 35 percent plus a 50 percent increase in bonus payments.
Matos said the agreement was aimed at contributing to the recovery of real wages which have fallen to 30 percent of the 1980 levels.

Under the agreement a Grade One public sector employee will earn 100,000 bolivars ($210) per month of which half is considered bonus payments, the release said. A blue collar worker will earn 97,000 bolivars ($204) of which 57,000 bolivars is considered bonus payments.
Salaries for other public sector grades will be raised proportionately, the release added.
Venezuela has been rocked by a series of protests and strikes by public sector workers over pay since the start of the year.
